notes: Start/finish gantry (Tripo H3.1 job 8a886b5d from art/codex/r5-plates/plate-gantry-34w.png, 18 credits). Metres at scale 1, origin = the footprint's bounding-box centre at the base (y = 0 on the sand; the racing surface is at y 0.5, so subtract 0.5 for heights over the road). x = across the track, y = up. Two galvanised scaffold towers in blue tarp, a box-truss girder with a TELUK banner and chequered ends, a timing board (00:00.0) on top, red-white flags. Clear opening between the towers 46.0 m (x -22.98..23.03): it spans Teluk's 44 m start straight (hw 22 at s = 0) with ~1 m to spare each side, so place it at scale 1. Girder underside 14.36 m, girder + bunting top 20.7 m (19.0-19.9 m away from the ends), the board 17.0-23.0 m over |x| < ~9 m, flag tips 25.9 m; girder depth z -2.40..+4.12 (the bounding box is centred on the towers and flags, not on the girder). front -z = the plate's face (the sharpest TELUK and 00:00.0): turn the gantry so -Z meets the racers on the run-in, i.e. city.js's span basis turned 180 deg: makeBasis(right.negate(), up, tan). Then the travel direction is +z and the girder slab runs a0 -2.40 .. a1 +4.12 along travel. With city.js's span basis unchanged (right, up, -tan) the run-in sees the +Z face: it also reads TELUK and 00:00.0, a little softer, with a faint ghost line under the banner. Both faces are fine for the finish camera. One mesh, one material (base 2048, ORM + normal 512, emissive 1024, WebP, meshopt high); cast shadows are optional (one instance). The timing board's orange digits glow: an emissive map made from the model's own texels (bright orange AND on the board's triangles, art/codex/r5-gantry/board_emis.py), emissive factor 1; raise emissiveIntensity for more bloom.
